rows: Maintenance Procedures Information System
Overhead Lines
Maintenance Procedures
Document No.: TL-032-r0a
Equipment: Overhead lines, 220 kV, 66 kV
Issued to: Networks
Status: Approved
Approval date: 07 December 2004
Procedure: Changing a single tension bridle, with the circuit disconnected and earthed
Next review date: December 2009

sections_en.text: The document was reviewed on 22 September 2004 by:
1. Eng. Abdel Sattar Ibrahim Ahmed, Head of the Maintenance Procedures Systems Development and Quality Control Sector
at the Egyptian Electricity Holding Company
2. Eng. Said Mahmoud El-Sheemy, General Manager of Extra High Voltage Lines, Cairo Region
3. Eng. Abdel Hadi Awad, General Manager of 66 kV Lines, Cairo Region
4. Eng. Khairy Abdel Aziz Attia, Manager of Giza Lines, Middle Egypt Region
5. Eng. Mohamed Qaoud Mahmoud, Manager of Nag Hammadi Lines, Upper Egypt Region

It is assumed that there is a tower carrying two 220 kV circuits, with one conductor per phase, and it is required to fit a bridle for one of the phases instead of the existing bridle, noting that the end connection on the tension tower for this phase has a ready lug to which the loop lug, to be compressed onto the end of the 'LOOP' conductor, is fixed. The document was approved at the session of 07 December 2004 of the MPIS coordinators of the Egyptian Electricity Transmission Company regions.

rows: The National Energy Control Centre shall be notified of the work to be carried out, specifying the line name and circuit number.
A work order shall be issued stating that the circuit has been disconnected and earthed from both sides.
Make sure the circuit is disconnected using the voltage indicator.
Inform the workers of the circuit to be worked on and distribute the flags and badges distinguishing the colour of the circuit among them.
Make sure all occupational safety and health equipment is fit for use and that the workers are wearing it.
Personnel shall not climb the towers until instructions have been received from the engineer in charge of the work.

Determine the work location and the work group on the travelling platform and the scaffold, so that it does not exceed 3 persons. Earth the work area with the appropriate earths before and after the work location.
Occupational safety and health equipment suitable for work on overhead lines.
1 hand line, a scaffold suitable for carrying out such work.
A complete tool bag, a horizontal movement device on the tower body.
Suitable slings, a suitable hydraulic press — suitable compression dies.
Hydraulic cutter, 2 loop lugs suitable for the cross-sectional area of the bridle conductor.
Wire brush for cleaning the conductor, safety ropes 16 mm2 at least and of suitable length.
Measuring tape, file, hammer, sandpaper, suitable shackles.
Chain hoist of suitable capacity, come-along.
A set of earths with tested insulating sticks.
One of the workers climbs the tower after wearing the safety belt, using the climbing rope, carrying a hand line, and fixes it to the tower body.
Fit a local earth on the conductor from the start and end of the bridle before opening the bridle, to discharge the charges in the line after opening the bridle.
The rest of the workers carrying out the work climb the tower body.
Raise the work equipment required onto the tower body.
Fix the scaffold used on the phase to be worked on correctly ('Figure No. 3').
Fit the safety ropes using the chain hoist and the come-along.
Remove the old LOOP from the side on which the scaffold is.
Repeat the same steps and remove the bridle from the other side of the same phase on the tension tower.
Lower the old bridle to the ground and bring a new conductor of the same length as the old bridle (Figure 1).
Then we start the process of manufacturing a new bridle.
After measuring the old LOOP and preparing a new conductor of the same length as the old LOOP.
Clean the inner surface of the bridle lug using sandpaper ('Figure No. 1').
Insert the conductor into the loop lug until the aluminium wire strands hit the bottom of the lug cavity.
Start compressing the loop lug from the bottom of the cylindrical cavity.
Continue the compression process, watching the compressions overlap one over the other by 10% until we reach the end of the joint.
Repeat the same steps at the second end of the LOOP.
After finishing all of them correctly, raise the LOOP to the top of the tower using the hand line (Figure No. 2).
Fix the new bridle in its place on its phase, using the scaffold fixed at the work location.
Repeat the same steps at the second end of the LOOP.
After finishing the work, lower the equipment used from the tower body.
Make sure all the workers carrying out the work have come down from the towers.
Remove the temporary earths fitted on the circuit worked on.
Notify the National Energy Control Centre that the work is finished, and it will reconnect the circuit.

Introduction
The document was reviewed on 22 September 2004 by:
1. Eng. Abdel Sattar Ibrahim Ahmed, Head of the Maintenance Procedures Systems Development and Quality Control Sector
at the Egyptian Electricity Holding Company
2. Eng. Said Mahmoud El-Sheemy, General Manager of Extra High Voltage Lines, Cairo Region
3. Eng. Abdel Hadi Awad, General Manager of 66 kV Lines, Cairo Region
4. Eng. Khairy Abdel Aziz Attia, Manager of Giza Lines, Middle Egypt Region
5. Eng. Mohamed Qaoud Mahmoud, Manager of Nag Hammadi Lines, Upper Egypt Region
It is assumed that there is a tower carrying two 220 kV circuits, with one conductor per phase, and it is required to fit a bridle for one of the phases instead of the existing bridle, noting that the end connection on the tension tower for this phase has a ready lug to which the loop lug, to be compressed onto the end of the 'LOOP' conductor, is fixed. The document was approved at the session of 07 December 2004 of the MPIS coordinators of the Egyptian Electricity Transmission Company regions.
Safety Precautions
The National Energy Control Centre shall be notified of the work to be carried out, specifying the line name and circuit number.
A work order shall be issued stating that the circuit has been disconnected and earthed from both sides.
Make sure the circuit is disconnected using the voltage indicator.
Inform the workers of the circuit to be worked on and distribute the flags and badges distinguishing the colour of the circuit among them.
Make sure all occupational safety and health equipment is fit for use and that the workers are wearing it.
Personnel shall not climb the towers until instructions have been received from the engineer in charge of the work.
Determine the work location and the work group on the travelling platform and the scaffold, so that it does not exceed 3 persons. Earth the work area with the appropriate earths before and after the work location.
Tools, Instruments and Equipment Used
Occupational safety and health equipment suitable for work on overhead lines.
1 hand line, a scaffold suitable for carrying out such work.
A complete tool bag, a horizontal movement device on the tower body.
Suitable slings, a suitable hydraulic press — suitable compression dies.
Hydraulic cutter, 2 loop lugs suitable for the cross-sectional area of the bridle conductor.
Wire brush for cleaning the conductor, safety ropes 16 mm2 at least and of suitable length.
Measuring tape, file, hammer, sandpaper, suitable shackles.
Chain hoist of suitable capacity, come-along.
A set of earths with tested insulating sticks.
Procedures to be Carried Out
One of the workers climbs the tower after wearing the safety belt, using the climbing rope, carrying a hand line, and fixes it to the tower body. | 1.
Fit a local earth on the conductor from the start and end of the bridle before opening the bridle, to discharge the charges in the line after opening the bridle. | 2.
The rest of the workers carrying out the work climb the tower body. | 3.
Raise the work equipment required onto the tower body. | 4.
Fix the scaffold used on the phase to be worked on correctly ('Figure No. 3'). | 5.
Fit the safety ropes using the chain hoist and the come-along. | 6.
Remove the old LOOP from the side on which the scaffold is. | 7.
Repeat the same steps and remove the bridle from the other side of the same phase on the tension tower. | 8.
Lower the old bridle to the ground and bring a new conductor of the same length as the old bridle (Figure 1). | 9.
Then we start the process of manufacturing a new bridle. | 10.
After measuring the old LOOP and preparing a new conductor of the same length as the old LOOP. | 11.
Clean the inner surface of the bridle lug using sandpaper ('Figure No. 1'). | 12.
Insert the conductor into the loop lug until the aluminium wire strands hit the bottom of the lug cavity. | 13.
Start compressing the loop lug from the bottom of the cylindrical cavity. | 14.
Continue the compression process, watching the compressions overlap one over the other by 10% until we reach the end of the joint. | 15.
Repeat the same steps at the second end of the LOOP. | 16.
After finishing all of them correctly, raise the LOOP to the top of the tower using the hand line (Figure No. 2). | 17.
Fix the new bridle in its place on its phase, using the scaffold fixed at the work location. | 18.
Repeat the same steps at the second end of the LOOP. | 19.
After finishing the work, lower the equipment used from the tower body. | 20.
Make sure all the workers carrying out the work have come down from the towers. | 21.
Remove the temporary earths fitted on the circuit worked on. | 22.
Notify the National Energy Control Centre that the work is finished, and it will reconnect the circuit. | 23.
